title: Learn hub: replace /templates with a unified learning catalog
description:
Problem: /templates (branch pse/adds-templates) was a bespoke blueprint-styled page, and the content strategy was too narrow.

Vision (expanded 2026-08-22): /learn is an IBM-Think-style editorial hub (reference: https://www.ibm.com/think) that unifies our learning and editorial content: templates, videos, tutorials, examples, workshops, blog articles, and upcoming comparisons/explainers. Phase 1 (tasks .1-.7): faceted catalog replacing /templates, shared design language, redirects, seeds. Phase 2 (tasks .8-.12): content strategy and IA (Fable 5), editorial design addendum (Fable 5), editorial landing at /learn with the catalog demoted to a browse surface, blog integration (model gated on a user ruling), and a comparison/explainer article pipeline.

Ordering: .8 -> .9 -> .10 -> .11; .12 after .8 and .9. Blog work (.11) additionally requires a recorded user ruling.

Orchestrated 2026-08-22/23 in 6 waves with per-ticket opus review and fable adversarial verify.

description:
Problem: user review (2026-08-24): on article detail pages the lead image is overly big; on a widescreen it is wild. The treatment must change, not just shrink.

File scope: the article detail layout under src/components/learn/ (ArticleLayout or its v2+ successor) and the article route.

Fix direction: cap the lead media so it never dominates a wide viewport: constrain it to the article text column width with a max height and object-fit cover, or per the design doc a split header (image beside title block) above a threshold; keep aspect ratio stable to avoid layout shift; small screens keep the current full-width behavior. Follow learn-editorial.md; if the doc lacks a widescreen media rule, add the chosen rule to the doc in the same change.

Verification: one image-heavy migrated article checked at 1440, 1920, and 2560 in light and dark: the image must not exceed the text column and viewport-height cap; npx eslint and yarn format:check.

Non-goals: landing or hub imagery, image pipeline changes.
closeReason: Article hero tamed: commit eb205d8b37 plus orchestrator nit-fix commit (sizes min-clause, harmonization D5 cross-ref). Hero capped to the 46rem prose measure with stable 16:9, choice grounded in D5 and documented as a learn-editorial.md 4.1 amendment; geometry verified at 1440/1920/2560 via iframe viewport override (browser resize unavailable in the sandbox - the cap is a static max-width so it holds by construction). Opus review pass.

comments.author: pascal
comments.text: Treatment chosen: constrain hero to the article text-column measure (max-w-[46rem], matching D5's prose cap), keeping aspect-video (16:9) so height is bounded (414px at the 736px cap) with no layout shift. Rejected the split-header alternative: ArticleLayout is explicitly a plain presentational shell shared by blog/comparison/explainer with a single-column composition (learn-editorial.md 4.1); a split header would restructure that shell's top matter for all three producers, well beyond this ticket's file scope, whereas capping the hero to the already-established 46rem prose measure is a one-line width change that makes the hero visually part of the same reading column instead of a wider banner floating above it. This supersedes learn-harmonization.md D5's hero breakout specifically (D5 still governs code blocks/figures); documented as a kbx.7 amendment in learn-editorial.md section 4.1 item 3. Verified at 1440/1920/2560 via a same-origin iframe width override (mcp playwright browser was locked by a concurrent agent's session the whole run, and the claude-in-chrome resize_window tool had no effect on this tab's actual viewport, pinned at 2092px by the window manager regardless of requested size) on /learn/articles/fusion (featuredImage): image renders at 736x414, flush with the prose column's left/right edges, never exceeding the article's max-w-5xl shell, no overflow. Small screens (375, 640) unaffected: image stays full-width under the 46rem cap.

title: Hero band: align column heights and baseline the more-links
description:
Problem: user review (2026-08-24): the three hero-band columns (latest articles left, featured center, latest videos right) end at visibly different heights. Requirement: articles and videos columns match in height at least roughly, and their trailing more-links (All articles / All videos) sit on the same vertical line.

File scope: the hero band components under src/components/learn/.

Fix direction: after kbx.5 lands the 5/1/2 composition, balance the columns: size video thumbnails/rows so 2 videos plus the link visually fill the same height as 5 article rows plus the link; pin both more-links to the column bottom (flex column with the link anchored) so they share a baseline; the featured column must not extend past the side columns.

Verification: browser measurement on the dev server at 1440 and 1920: bounding boxes of the two more-links share the same y within a few px, column heights within a small tolerance; screenshots light and dark; npx eslint and yarn format:check.

Non-goals: changing the 5/1/2 counts, hub pages (kbx.6).
closeReason: Hero band balanced: commits 63d7df048c, 89565129d3, 468600b4e2. All-articles/All-videos links share an identical baseline (0px delta measured on /learn and both verified hubs), featured column bounded by the grid wrapper, hub spacing re-verified per the inherited kbx.6 ruling, yarn build green (540 pages). Opus review pass.

comments.author: pascal
comments.text: NEEDS-PASCAL: /learn/topics/tooling-observability has only 1 qualifying video (youtubeId-bearing) for its rail, not 2 - a pre-existing data-availability gap (confirmed via git-stash before/after: 'All videos'/'All articles' delta was 386.68px(1440)/341.68px(1920) BEFORE my fix, 311.12px both widths AFTER - improved, not caused, by this change). My fix (fixed lg:h-[210px] thumbnail, calibrated for the 2-video case) can't close this gap without either a grotesquely stretched single thumbnail or added component complexity to size thumbnails by video count. Chose to leave it as a recorded, pre-existing content-availability limitation rather than engineer a bespoke per-count sizing fix, since the ticket frames this work around the 5/1/2 composition (which /learn and /learn/topics/graphql-federation both have, and both now align within ~1px at 1440/1920). | chose: ship the fixed-height fix for the standard 2-video case; leave the 1-video hub misalignment as a known, unresolved edge case for follow-up (either backfill a 2nd qualifying video for that hub, or a separate ticket to make LearnLatestVideos size gracefully for 1 vs 2 rows).

comments.author: pascal
comments.text: NEEDS-PASCAL: correction plan for kbx.8 applied - reverted LearnLatestVideos.tsx thumbnail to full aspect-video (no fixed lg:h-[210px]), and in LearnEditorialBand.tsx made the rail column xl:flex xl:flex-col with xl:mt-auto on the LearnTagCloud wrapper (the last child), anchoring the tag cloud to the column bottom at xl. Because LearnTagCloud renders below the 'All videos' link, this does NOT put 'All videos' on the same baseline as 'All articles' - only the tag cloud's bottom edge is now flush with the column bottom. Making 'All videos' itself baseline-align with 'All articles' requires either moving LearnTagCloud above the link or accepting the tag cloud as the anchored block; per the correction plan this is left as your design decision, no fixed pixel height was reintroduced. | chose: apply the structural xl:flex/xl:mt-auto anchor to the trailing block (tag cloud) as literally specified, without deciding the tag-cloud-vs-link placement question.

comments.author: pascal
comments.text: Applied the correction plan (single-link version, per the plan's stated preference): moved 'All videos' ArrowLink out of LearnLatestVideos into LearnEditorialBand's rail column, rendered after LearnTagCloud, xl:flex xl:flex-col + xl:mt-auto xl:pt-6 on both more-links; gated the videos wrapper on latestVideos.length>0; Latest column got xl:flex xl:flex-col too. Commit 468600b4e2, files: LearnEditorialBand.tsx (+17-5), LearnLatestVideos.tsx (+8-5, ArrowLink import removed, doc comment updated) - net diff vs eb205d8b37 touches both files (finding 4 resolved). Gates: tsc/eslint/prettier/yarn build all clean. NEEDS-PASCAL: could not hit exact 1440/1920 viewport widths for browser verification - Playwright MCP was locked ('Browser is already in use') by a concurrent process for the whole session, and the claude-in-chrome extension window would not resize below/above a fixed ~1888x895 (resize_window calls succeeded but had no effect past the first). Measured instead at the only achievable width, 1888px (still within the xl/2xl range the fix targets, since none of the changed rules are 2xl-scoped) on /learn, /learn/topics/graphql-federation, and /learn/topics/tooling-observability (the 1-video edge case from kbx.5's comment). Results: 'All articles'/'All videos' y-delta is 0px on all three pages (exact match, down from the 311px gap noted in kbx.5's comment even for the 1-video hub); featured column content never exceeds the grid-stretched wrapper height on any page (no overflow past side columns). Dark-theme screenshots confirm visually. | chose: report real measurements at the only width the environment allowed rather than fabricate 1440/1920 numbers; flagging the tooling gap for a human or a later run when the browser tools are free.

title: Watch section: 4 videos per row
description:
Problem: user review (2026-08-24): the video cards in the landing Watch section are far too big; two per row wastes space. Four fit easily per row on desktop.

File scope: the Watch section grid/card components under src/components/learn/.

Fix direction: 4 columns at desktop widths, scaling down sensibly (e.g. 2 at tablet, 1 at mobile) without reintroducing the lg orphan-row problem fixed in kbx.4 (verify the intermediate breakpoints produce full rows: prefer counts that divide evenly at each breakpoint). Card content scales with the smaller footprint (thumbnail, duration badge, kicker, title; drop the dek if it no longer fits cleanly).

Verification: browser check at 1280, 1440, 1920: 4 per row at desktop, no orphan rows at the chosen breakpoints, thumbnails and duration badges intact, light and dark; npx eslint and yarn format:check.

Non-goals: hero-band video column (kbx.8), video detail pages, video data.
closeReason: Watch 4-up grid landed: commit 45b5fc4f92. Additive CardGrid skipThreeCol prop gives sm:2 / lg:4 with no 3-col step (orphan-free for 4 items); 4-up from lg after a 1024px legibility check (~214px cards, dek kept); /learn/browse grids proven unaffected (prop not passed, grep-verified). Opus review pass; minors are documented trade-offs (dark-mode note moot: site is single-theme dark; storybook gap pre-existing).

comments.author: pascal
comments.text: Decision: 4-up starts at lg (1024px), not xl. Simulated a 1024px viewport (wrapper-width + forced grid-template-columns test against the live 3200 dev server) and measured ~214px card width: thumbnail 164x92, VIDEO badge, HOT CHOCOLATE kicker, 2-3 line title, and the tagline/dek (line-clamp-3) all render legibly with no clipping - screenshot confirmed. Kept the dek; no need to drop it. Added CardGrid.skipThreeCol (additive, default false) rather than a new step value: cols=4 progressive + skipThreeCol renders sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4, skipping the lg:grid-cols-3 orphan step from kbx.4. /learn/browse's two cols=4 progressive grids (LearnCatalog, LearnCardSkeleton) don't pass skipThreeCol and are confirmed unchanged (still sm:2 lg:3 xl:4, computed 3 cols verified live). tsc/eslint/prettier all pass.

title: Extract Mocha examples into the platform-examples repository
description:
Problem: user direction (2026-08-24): the new repo https://github.com/ChilliCream/platform-examples.git collects platform examples. All Mocha examples move out of graphql-platform into it, each as a planned move. Requirements: a SINGLE Directory.Packages.props at the repo root; examples live under examples/Mocha/<Name>/; each example gets a description page as BOTH a README.md in the repo AND a learn example entry on the website.

Source inventory (verified in src/Mocha/examples/): Demo (6 projects, has README), PostgresTransport (6 projects, Aspire AppHost), AzureEventHubTransport (6 project folders but NO .csproj files, broken/incomplete: needs reconstruction or a ruling), AotExample (3 projects), ExceptionPolicies (1 project). Explicitly OUT of scope: src/Mocha/src/Examples/ (18 snippet projects referenced by website/content/docs/mocha pages; moving them breaks docs).

Workspace: clone the repo to ~/code/platform-examples if not present. Git policy: create commits in platform-examples per move on a branch, do NOT push without user approval; graphql-platform-side deletions stay uncommitted in the worktree per standing policy.

Children: .1 repo scaffold, .2-.6 one planned move per example, .7 website learn entries for the moved examples.

title: platform-examples scaffold: root Directory.Packages.props and layout
description:
Problem: the fresh platform-examples repo needs its skeleton before any example moves in.

File scope: the platform-examples clone (~/code/platform-examples) only.

Fix direction: root files: Directory.Packages.props (central package management, ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true; seed the package versions the five Mocha examples reference, taking versions from graphql-platform's root Directory.Packages.props), Directory.Build.props (LangVersion/nullable/implicit usings consistent with graphql-platform conventions), global.json matching graphql-platform's SDK, .gitignore (dotnet standard), .editorconfig copied from graphql-platform, root README.md describing the repo purpose and the examples/<Product>/<Name> layout, empty examples/Mocha/ directory established by the first move. A solution file per product (examples/Mocha/Mocha.Examples.slnx) or one root slnx: pick one, document in the README.

Verification: dotnet build on the (still example-less) solution succeeds or trivially no-ops; files present; commit created on a branch, not pushed.

Non-goals: moving any example, CI workflows (later, needs user input on runners).

description:
